from.place: The assertion that the category of discrete G-modules has enough injectives, supplied by the cited functorial-embedding lemma

title: Discrete modules with continuous action have functorial injective embeddings
statement: Let $G$ be a profinite group and $A$ a finite ring. In the category $\mathcal C$ of left $A$-modules with a $G$-action by $A$-linear automorphisms such that every element has open stabilizer, with $A$-linear $G$-equivariant maps, there is a functor $J:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ and a natural transformation $j:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}\to J$ such that each $j_M:M\to J(M)$ is a monomorphism and $J(M)$ is injective. Consequently every object of $\mathcal C$ embeds in an injective object, so $\mathcal C$ has enough injectives in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions].
